facts.value: Rejected infant baptism and baptized believers on confession of faith. Many rejected oaths and the holding of civil office.

citations.excerpt: Voluntary baptism of adult and responsible converts is, therefore, the only valid baptism.
This restoration included the rejection of oaths and capital punishment and the abstention from the exercise of magistracy.

facts.value: Groups that, from the time of Luther's break with Rome, denied the validity of infant baptism. The name, meaning re-baptizers, was given by opponents and generally rejected by those it described.

citations.excerpt: ANABAPTISTS (“re-baptizers,” from Gr. ἀνά and βαπτίζω ), a name given by their enemies to various sects which on the  occasion of Luther’s revolt from Romanism denied the validity of infant baptism
The designation was generally repudiated by those to whom it was applied

facts.value_before_verify: Radical Reformation groups that denied the validity of infant baptism. The name, meaning re-baptizers, was given by opponents and generally rejected by those it described.

research_notes: CE 1913 dates Anabaptism to the Zwickau prophets 1521; EB1911 and Schaff place first believers' baptism at Zurich 1525. Modern scholarship generally distinguishes the Zwickau prophets from Swiss Brethren; ODCC check needed.
